title: Lease-End Broom-Swept vs. White-Glove Commercial Turnover Costs
seoTitle: Broom Swept Office Cleaning Cost: Lease-End Rates vs. White-Glove
metaDescription: Broom swept office cleaning cost averages $0.10–$0.22/sq ft ($35–$65/hr) vs. $0.25–$0.45/sq ft white-glove. Audit lease clauses and open our calculator.
excerpt: Decode how US commercial landlords define broom-swept condition versus white-glove lease surrender—and what each tier costs per square foot. Use these labor-hour benchmarks and deposit-protection steps to avoid inflated landlord back-charges.
quickAnswer: Broom swept office cleaning cost averages $0.10 to $0.22 per square foot ($35 to $65 per standard labor hour, with a $90 to $135 minimum visit floor), whereas a white-glove commercial lease-end turnover runs $0.25 to $0.45 per square foot ($55 to $95 per specialty hour). For a 5,000 sq ft suite with two restrooms, broom-swept surrender typically costs $550 to $1,150 compared to $1,350 to $2,250 for full white-glove restoration.

blocks.text: In US commercial real estate, the surrender clause at the back of your office lease carries five-figure financial consequences if misread. Most standard leases obligate departing tenants to deliver the premises in **"broom-swept condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted,"** yet property managers routinely withhold security deposits when suites fail subjective white-glove walk-throughs.

Knowing the exact pricing boundary between broom-swept prep and full [office move-in/move-out deep cleaning](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/office-move-in-move-out-cleaning-cost/) prevents two costly mistakes: paying $2,000+ for white-glove detailing a landlord plans to demolish anyway, or under-cleaning a suite and getting hit with a landlord's marked-up **$75 to $110 per hour** restoration back-charge.
Broom-Swept vs. White-Glove Pricing Across Suite Sizes

Because broom-swept service focuses on gross debris clearance, full floor vacuuming, damp mopping of hard surfaces, and basic trash removal, trained crews maintain near-standard ISSA production speeds (**2,400 to 3,200 sq ft per hour**) billed at **$35 to $65 per standard labor hour**. White-glove turnovers add interior cabinet degreasing, glass adhesive scraping, baseboard washing, and carpet extraction, shifting billing into the **$55 to $95 per specialty hour** bracket.

blocks.title: Ask If the Next Tenant Is Triggering a Demolition Build-Out
blocks.text: Before ordering $0.35/sq ft carpet extraction or VCT waxing, ask your leasing agent in writing whether the landlord plans to gut and re-carpet the suite for the incoming tenant. If demolition is scheduled, document the lease's broom-swept language and spend only on debris removal, vacuuming, and damp mopping.
What Commercial Leases Actually Mean by Broom-Swept

Although "broom-swept" sounds informal, commercial lease law interprets it strictly: all personal property, furniture, cabling, signage, and loose trash must be removed, floors must be vacuumed or swept free of dust and food debris, sinks and toilets must be flushed and free of gross soil, and surfaces must be left sanitary enough for broker showings. Comparing deliverables side by side clarifies what you are buying.

blocks.text: Operational Equipment for Fast Lease-End Cleanouts

Lease-end crews work on tight final-day deadlines between the moving truck pulling away at 2:00 PM and the landlord key handoff at 5:00 PM. Lightweight, durable commercial equipment lets two technicians clear multiple suites and stairwells rapidly without stalling on heavy cord changes or leaky buckets—critical when working out of a [traditional vs. high-capacity janitorial cart](/janitorial-carts-mops-and-tools/rubbermaid-high-capacity-cart-vs-6173-traditional/).

items: **Lightweight Multi-Floor Debris Pickup:** The **Oreck Commercial Pro6A Backpack Vacuum** (6 qt capacity, Micro-Filter filtration, 10.5 lb chassis, 67 dBA rating) speeds final vacuum passes across vacated cubicles, interior stairwells, and closet alcoves.

**High-Capacity Hard-Floor Rinse:** For long VCT hallways and tiled lobbies above 5,000 sq ft, the **Rubbermaid Commercial WaveBrake 35-Quart Down-Press Mop Bucket** (35 qt capacity, WaveBrake baffling, Down-Press wringer, Quiet Casters) pairs with a dirty-water divider option to clear tracked mover boot prints in one pass.

**Compact Small-Suite Mobility:** For smaller 1,500 to 5,000 sq ft lease surrenders with tight janitorial closets or passenger-elevator access, the **O-Cedar Commercial MaxiPlus 26-Quart Wringer Combo** (26 qt capacity, Side-Press wringer, 3-in Casters, Compact footprint) packs easily into a service van and eliminates unnecessary water weight.

blocks.title: Beware of Abandoned Decommissioning Debris Penalties
blocks.text: Commercial cleaning bids assume an empty suite. If departing staff leave behind broken task chairs, boxes of binders, or server-rack cardboard, janitorial vendors will either refuse broom-swept sign-off or bill $55 to $95 per hour plus municipal haul-off surcharges—costing far less than a landlord's $500+ dumpster penalty.
When Broom-Swept Cleaning Triggers Landlord Back-Charges

Even when a lease specifies broom-swept delivery, landlords routinely deduct from security deposits when departing tenants leave behind sticky floor-mat adhesive, un-emptied breakroom refrigerators, or heavy black caster marks on **VCT/LVT vinyl (1.04x)** and **ceramic tile and grout (1.12x)** corridors. Because building management companies dispatch their own preferred union or contract crew at **$75 to $110 per hour** plus a 15% administrative markup, paying **$150 to $350** upfront for targeted appliance cleanouts and heel-mark scrubbing prevents $800+ in post-lease deductions.
Protecting Your Security Deposit During Final Walk-Throughs

Landlord holdbacks happen when cleaning scope is verbal rather than photographed. Whether you manage an entire floor or oversee a [shared common-area suite split](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/shared-suite-common-area-cleaning-cost-split/), executing a documented handover turns cleaning into a verified deposit shield.

items.name: Audit Exact Lease Surrender Wording
items.text: Highlight every phrase in your lease's Surrender and Repairs sections—specifically noting whether carpet shampooing or wall painting is required or waived.

items.name: Solicit Two Line-Item Quotes Against Lease Scope
items.text: Give bidders the exact square footage, restroom count, and floor types from your [office cleaning cost guide](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) benchmarks so bids separate broom-swept base labor from optional extraction.

items.name: Verify COI Before Moving-Out Week
items.text: Ensure your selected cleaner's Certificate of Insurance remains active through your final lease date so security does not block building entry.

items.name: Time-Stamp Photo Proof Before Returning Keys
items.text: Capture wide-angle photos of every corner, restroom, and kitchenette once cleaning finishes, and obtain a signed walk-through receipt from the property manager.

faqs.q: Does a broom-swept cleaner still need a Certificate of Insurance (COI)?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial building owners require a valid COI naming the landlord and property management firm as Additional Insured—typically with $1,000,000/$2,000,000 Commercial General Liability and statutory Workers' Compensation—even for a 3-hour final sweep on your last day of occupancy.

faqs.q: What OSHA compliance checks matter during lease decommissioning cleans?
faqs.a: Under OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200), contractors must bring properly labeled chemical bottles and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) into vacated suites. If old medical drawers, clogged restroom backups, or sharp broken glass are present, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) PPE rules apply.

faqs.q: Should we request Green Seal GS-37 chemicals for a broom-swept surrender?
faqs.a: Using Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice neutral cleaners leaves zero harsh ammonia or solvent odor during the landlord's walk-through inspection and satisfies LEED-certified building management policies at little to no added labor cost.

faqs.q: Which lease-end tasks are excluded from broom-swept commercial cleaning bids?
faqs.a: Broom-swept quotes exclude furniture decommissioning, IT low-voltage cable removal, drywall patching, touch-up painting, ceiling tile swaps, and deep stain or burn-mark carpet patching. Those belong to general contractors or decommissioning movers.

faqs.q: Can our existing 4.333-week janitorial vendor handle our final-day broom-swept clean?
faqs.a: Often yes, and at lower mobilization cost. However, because monthly contracts spread visits across 4.333 weeks per month for light occupied upkeep, your vendor will still issue a final one-time invoice ($0.10 to $0.22/sq ft) for extended post-mover floor and bin clearing.
